answer: Decentralized AI networks resist Sybil attacks by combining stake-weighted cryptographic challenges with hardware attestation. To participate, an agent must broadcast a verified signal of non-trivial execution on dedicated chips, forming a ferrous barrier against zero-cost identity replication. Under this regime, a velvet slashing mechanism softly erodes the stake of inactive or duplicate nodes, forcing attackers to sustain unbearable real-world hardware and capital expenditures to dilute consensus.
